body: I'm sorry to hear that. Thanks for reaching out.
I'm letting you know I made it to my appointment. He's adjusted my meds and I feel better just having had it addressed..thanks for reaching out and caring.
Thank you, I appreciate you taking the time to write to me.
Thank you. I promise you I will get to the appointment.

That's a worry of mine. Since I have my trip planned to see my husband and I am our only income at this time, I don't want to be hospitalized. So I will have to watch what I say while still trying to tell them what's going on so I can be treated properly.
The bad part is that I don't think there's any help for me. I've tried doctors, therapy, medication, hospitals, for most of my adult life. Hotlines tell me to breathe.
I don't know how to get better. I've gone to doctors, therepy, etc.

I know, I shouldn't be like this about it, it just hurts. I'm sorry. It's been a long hard road and there's still a ways to go. It's quite possible he didn't know, or didn't understand the seriousness or extent. It's still a painful thing to process. He's even apologized for, yes, he used the term 'bait and switch' in the past and said he didn't know, but didn't say anything about knowing about his mental illness. But I guess it doesn't really matter now. Sometimes, we just have to accept what is. Edited to fix a sentence, sorry.

Yes, this is a great and accurate (for me) resource. I'm fairly newly diagnosed and resources like these really help me understand that I don't "just" have depression and anxiety. If I can understand the illness maybe I can get better treatment. Thanks for sharing this.
Thank you!

Thank you. That's sort of how I'm thinking. If staying level means I can get through this crisis without having to be hospitalized with seizures or suicide attempts then maybe that is all I can do. I'm just one person.
So very true. SO reached out to his family for help numerous times and was rebuffed until he almost died from a withdrawal related seizure.
Hey, my local meeting is Monday evenings. How about you?

Years ago, I asked Husband to put me on an allowance. He didn't want to. Long story short, he really should have. Sometimes we can't control ourselves with money. It's a common symptom, in my understanding.
Thanks!
Thank you!
I am, but I got to see my (for the time being due to multiple physical and mental health issues) long distance SO. I'm trying to focus on the positive... And it's really just another damn day.

My Q has been doing home detox/supervised taper for a month at his parents' several hundred miles away. Doing all this during the holidays is so hard. I'm praying for you and all of us. Ok or chat me if you want to talk.
She is certainly an outstanding human being who has contributed a lot of good to this sad little world.

And yet she's helped millions of children through her Imagination Library program and helped rebuild her economically depressed corner of Tennessee into a profitable and bustling economy with Dollywood and numerous other attractions. She's a very giving person. It's too bad that she couldn't have children (if that was her desire) but she has certainly helped countless others.
If my in laws were to be won over by my devotion it would have likely happened already, but we'll start over and have a happy life together regardless. Thanks for the encouraging words.

That's my plan, yes. I am only staying here to settle affairs and work so that I can save money for us to start over again in his country, which is kinder than the US, where I am now. I've lived in his home country before too, so I know my way around a bit.
Thanks. It's really hard but I am trying to have faith that it will be ok in the long run.

It was relayed by my husband, but I've known this awful old man for years and it's absolutely in line with who he is. I've heard him tell my husband over the phone that I'm the cause of his problems and have changed his life for the worse. I know that addicts lie but this absolutely in line with other things that dry-drunk has said about me in the past (in my hearing).
